propositions: Cancelled ACLI link-delete commands (EOF on stdin at confirmation prompt) are counted as applied links, fabricating success in batch_outcome and evading silent-divergence canary detection.

The except CalledProcessError handler in _update_one_dispatch_links increments links_applied without distinguishing genuine idempotent races (404/409/not-found) from deterministic failures like command-cancelled, producing permanent silent divergence.
The --yes flag accepted by acli 1.3.19-stable link subcommands is not passed, causing the confirmation prompt to read EOF and report command cancelled on every reconciliation pass.
The narrowed idempotent check must inspect both stderr and stdout (not stderr alone) to correctly identify concurrent-removal races, mirroring the delete_issue precedent in acli.py:739.
A new links_failed counter and corrected idempotent detection will expose actual failures in batch_outcome and restore canary visibility without breaking benign concurrent-removal races.
